My academic background combines biotechnology,
bioinformatics and computational biology with
research in animal genetics and genomics.

My current research focuses on the integration
of genomic and metabolomic data to investigate
molecular phenotypes and complex traits in
livestock. I am also extending these approaches
towards AI-assisted phenotyping and the integration
of digital and molecular phenomic data.

## <i class="bi bi-award cv-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i> Selected Academic Highlights

::: {.cv-highlights}

**MSCA Postdoctoral Global Fellowship — ABPhenomics (2027–2030)**

Awarded a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
Postdoctoral Global Fellowship for research
integrating artificial intelligence, digital
phenotyping, metabolomics and genomic information
to investigate pig behaviour and animal welfare.

[ABPhenomics project](projects/abphenomics/index.qmd) |
[European Commission — CORDIS](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101282544)

---

**COST Action CA22112 — European Network on Livestock Phenomics (EU-LI-PHE)**

Member of two working groups:

- **WG2 — Genome to phenome integration**
- **WG3 — Computational resources and methodologies for data analyses**

The network promotes the development, integration
and application of phenotyping approaches and
computational methodologies in livestock research.

[EU-LI-PHE website](https://eu-li-phe.eu/) |
[EU-LI-PHE CA22112](https://www.cost.eu/actions/CA22112/)

---

**Session Co-Chair — AI4AS 2026**

Co-Chair of **Session 4: AI for Science** at
the 2nd EAAP Artificial Intelligence for
Animal Science Conference (AI4AS),
Ghent, Belgium, 29–30 June 2026.

The conference addressed applications of
artificial intelligence and computational
methods in animal science.

[AI4AS website](https://ai4as.eaap.org/)

:::

## <i class="bi bi-book cv-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i> Teaching and Student Supervision

### Applied Genomics

**Lecturer | MSc in Bioinformatics,
University of Bologna | 2020–Present**

Teaching activities focus on the theoretical
and practical analysis of genomic data,
including SNP genotyping arrays,
next-generation sequencing datasets
and bioinformatic workflows.

### Thesis Supervision

Supervisor and co-supervisor of BSc and MSc
thesis projects involving bioinformatics,
genomics, computational biology and
multi-omics data analysis.

Research topics include genome-wide association
studies, genomic data mining, gene networks,
molecular phenotypes and computational methods
for biological data interpretation.

Previously, I served as a didactic tutor
for the Laboratory of Bioinformatics 1
at the University of Bologna (2014–2017).

## <i class="bi bi-people cv-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i> Scientific Networks and Community Activities

### COST EU-LI-PHE

Active participation in the European Network
on Livestock Phenomics (CA22112), with
involvement in WG2 and WG3.
Scientific activities include international
collaboration, short-term scientific mobility,
conference participation and meeting organisation.
I also served as Co-Chair of the Young Researchers
and Innovators session at the EU-LI-PHE
3rd Annual Meeting (Istanbul, 2026).

### Conference Presentations and Scientific Roles

I regularly contribute to international scientific
conferences and meetings, including WCGALP,
EAAP, ISAG, AI4AS and COST EU-LI-PHE activities.
My contributions include oral presentations
on animal genomics, molecular phenomics,
metabolomics and computational biology,
as well as session chairing and scientific
event organisation.

A selection of conference presentations,
scientific roles and upcoming events is
available on my [Events](events.qmd) page.


### Scientific Event Organisation

Member of organising or local committees
for scientific events, including:

- EU-LI-PHE 1st Annual Meeting (2024).
- Agritech Spoke 1 Workshop (2024).
- PigPhenomics Final Workshop (2023).
- Bologna Winter Schools in Bioinformatics.

## <i class="bi bi-lightbulb cv-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i> Entrepreneurship and Knowledge Transfer

**2020–2023 | Co-Founder and Data Scientist — GRIFFA SRL**

[GRIFFA](https://www.linkedin.com/company/griffa-srl/) was a biotechnology startup and
spin-off of the University of Bologna.

Its activities focused on DNA-based food
authentication and traceability, together
with applications of genetic analysis
to environmental monitoring.

This experience provided an opportunity
to apply genomic and bioinformatic
methodologies beyond academic research.
